messages:
jamal: Heads up — noticed a tail regression after yesterday's cohorting PR (r-infer#4123). p99 gen latency climbed ~90ms on the prod harness. overall GPU busy is about the same. KV miss-rate jumped ~1.4x. link: https://perf.example/run/1765439988
alex: Ugh. Can you paste the perf counters / flamegraph snippet or upload the microbench output? Which node pool saw this?@maria any ideas?
jamal: microbench summary pasted below (trimmed):
```
run: prod-harness-2026-06-10
p50: 18ms -> 22ms
p95: 72ms -> 120ms
p99: 110ms -> 200ms
kv_miss_rate: 0.9% -> 1.27%
note: spikes correlate with short decode bursts after prefill handshake
```
observed spikes coincide with a bunch of small decode batches (<= 32 tokens) getting mixed into the large-kernel path.
maria: reading that — smells like the queue/handshake shuffle we changed. The cohorting change rebalanced token_budget and handshake windows; decode flows might be starved or causing prefill to back off. Suggestion: separate decode into its own queue with token_budget=32, prefill cap=128, and KV priming window=10s. Also reduce prefill max_wait to 2ms for decode queue to avoid tiny batches.
sophia: ran a local canary with those knobs (10 runs, stable seed). Command used:
```
./bench --scenario=prod-harness --overrides "scheduler.decode.queue=decode-cohort,scheduler.decode.token_budget=32,scheduler.prefill.max_tokens=128,scheduler.decode.max_wait_ms=2,kv.priming.window_s=10"
```
10-run median: p99 improved vs post-PR: -40ms, but still +20ms vs baseline. GPU util up ~6%.
alex: kernel angle — small decode batches are hitting the generic large-batch kernel path, which triggers an extra kernel selection step and sometimes the kernel fallback path (small->large fallback). That adds ~10-40ms depending on handover. We should prefer a small-batch kernel for stage=decode and only use large kernel when batch_tokens > 256. Proposal:
```
scheduler.kernel_affinity.rules = [
  {stage: "decode", prefer: "small_kernel", min_tokens: 0, max_tokens: 255},
  {stage: "decode", prefer: "large_kernel", min_tokens: 256}
]
```
This avoids selection churn.
jamal: good call. I also saw KV cache drain spikes during burst windows — likely because decode cohorts don't prime KV; they pull from model cold and cause extra memory traffic. Maybe increase kv_warmup_tokens for decode cohort to 8 or prefetch first key ranges.
maria: combining ideas: hybrid approach — cohort decode into separate priority queue with token_cap=32 and aggressive priming (kv.prefetch_tokens=8). Also change batch_formation heuristic for decode to favor batch_count (like prefer combining up to 8 small requests) rather than strict token_count to avoid 1-2 request tiny kernels. That should stabilize kernel paths and reduce selection overhead.
sophia: I pushed a scheduler patch prototype and re-ran the bench. Patch snippet:
```
// scheduler: prefer batch_count for decode cohort
if (flow.stage == DECODE && batch.total_tokens < 64) {
  batch_heuristic = BATCH_BY_COUNT;
}
```
Bench (canary knobs + kernel_affinity + kv_prefetch=8): p99 is now within baseline ±5ms on the harness, p50/p95 stable. Throughput for high concurrency scenarios dropped ~2% and GPU mem usage rose slightly.
perf-bot: automated perf run 1765440400 completed:
- baseline (pre-PR): p99=110ms
- post-PR (r-infer#4123): p99=200ms
- canary (hybrid decode queue + kernel_affinity): p99=115ms
additional metrics: kv_miss_rate back to 0.95%, kernel_switch_count down 72%
alex: roll plan: canary 10% us-west, 4h probe. Tag traces with cohort=decode. Alerts: p99 > baseline+30ms or kv_miss_rate > 1.5x. Owners: jamal/maria/sophia. I'll open rollout PR + revert doc if canary fails.
jamal: assigning follow-ups:
- jamal: monitor canary, collect flamegraphs (4h)
- maria: terraform for queue + metrics tagging PR
- sophia: finish kernel affinity patch + unit tests
- alex: rollout PR + alert rules
Thanks all :thumbsup:
